notes.title: 1.1.08 out
notes.content: Minor push today that updates SteamVR libs and changes the way the syncrhronization happens with the compositor hoping that will fix the black screen on the headset issue some people are seeing.  Please let me know using the forums.

Hello Everyone!

Thanks to all of you who reported some issues on the forums.

This small update includes:
- Update to the latest SteamVR
- Update build environment
- Fixes to the way the compositor pipeline works, which should fix the issues some of you were reporting after some of the later updates
- Bouncy issue with moving the world when using a controller other than the Vive
- Allow disabling the internal HDR post-processing step (pressing "J" on the keyboard while focused on the mirror window will do this).  This may help some people who still run into issues.

Please keep the feedback coming!

Thanks,
F

notes.title: V1.1.02 Released
notes.content:
Hello Everyone!

Little big release...

Bug Fixes:
- SAVE button will now work again for models that had a rig coming in.  This has been reported in the forums, so thank you for all of you who found that.
- SAVE will now default to the FBX default, which is FBX binary.  The usual suspects (Unity, Blender) can load these.

Features:
- Rigging is now using GPU compute - still not that much better than before, but a huge overhaul under the covers.  

Enjoy and please keep posting issues as you find them.

Cheers,
F

notes.title: v1.1.0 Released! Now with Rigging
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

This update has enough in to be considered the first minor version increase. 
Here's what's new:

[h1]Selection Improvements:[/h1]
- fixed an issue that made manipulation with Oculus hard
- laser pointer now indicates the position of manipulation
- you can now select between multiple bones that start from the same position
- bone targetting is more precise
- when the model is in see-through mode, the bone that would be actuated is now highlited
- when manipulating a bone there will be a proportionally sized axis at the center of rotation
- Support for multiple hierarchy roots: e.g. a character that has accesories like weapons [url=https://www.cgtrader.com/free-3d-models/character/woman/medieval-woman-warrior]like this one[/url]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/a3df7b05ae08385c658a22ba22bf9bca1ffe1f69.png[/img]
(new bone highlight and controller selection)


[h1]File Loading Improvements:[/h1]
- improved support for FBX models with multiple parts - e.g.  [url=https://sketchfab.com/models/60c55714a337468db2d129095eec264a]this[/url]
- improved support for binding pose
- improved material transparency
- improved loading of HDR files with very high range 


[h1]New Major Feature: Rigging[/h1]
Models without skeletons will now load into the new rigging mode. I've added new sample model to illustrate rigging: rigging_hero_female.obj which comes from [url=https://sketchfab.com/models/3c31c9a2613e47a480103c9cb35cf8c2]here[/url].  

The new rigging menus look like this:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/e2486678cb571b6037684c2865e6d2fc91f035fc.png[/img]

To begin rigging, look for the hierarchy root, the white ball at about the center of the model with additional extra smaller balls around it. 
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/ad1c30df851c062827cf2de92dabf38badc39732.png[/img]

The green ball at the top will produce a single new node that is locked to the major axis, intenteded to create the spine.  The two blue balls to the sides will create two new nodes that have central symetry, intended for limbs - the mirrored node is created and updated automatically.

(dragging the green ball to create a spine node)
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/987eb25daf61bf525e36fb6e90a151d0480564de.png[/img]
(releasing to show the new spine node)
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/ae452a7b8d7cd094d1d7a85cefdb4dbba95e66f6.png[/img]

You can select and move any node to update its position.  Any node that begins life on the central axis will stay locked to that axis.  Any child node of a mirror link will produce a child of the correct mirror node (i.e. left elbow will produce a right elbow as a child of the right shoudler).

You can delete nodes by selecting the red ball below the node.  The red ball will only appear at the end of the chain, and you can't delete the root.

Because of the symetry controls, rigging assumes that the model is symetrical on the X axis, that is the YZ plane is the mirror.  In order to support models that may be aligned differently there are new mesh controls that will help you orient your model's meshes to this configuration while rigging. These transforms will only last while doing the rigging process so as to keep the model's original frame of reference.

Once your new skeleton is aligned with your mesh, hit the apply to mesh button :
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/279c282ef05942a2d2f793851891c6410a45eff6.png[/img]

... the model will now turn solid and will be ready to animate.
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/3b65e06c1b560709143ebcc44dd4b974a6afd4d4.png[/img]

There's also a Load and Save buttons on the Rig Control menu - these will save the state of your rig to a file that matches your model's file name (model.fbx will generate model.merprig).
For the time being, there's only one per file and you don't get any warnings around it. The new sample model comes with a pre-made rig that you can load using this button.

Finally, the rigging method is doing a simple nearest vertext to bone search, using a single bone per vertex.  This is far from state of the art but it is simple and easy to understand.  I wanted to focus on releasing the user interface and workflow to the community first and wait for feedback on the feature before diving deeper into refining that.

And with everything here, you can of course save back your model and use it wherever you want (minor note on that: the .obj file provided will be saved as .fbx)

Please keep commenting on the forums and let me know what your expericences are with the new features.  I hope you like them.

Cheers,
F

notes.title: 3DRudder Support - a must have for all seated VR experiences
notes.content:
Hi Everyone,

For some of you who may already own a 3DRudder, you may have noticed this has actually been supported for a few versions now. 

If you don't know what that is, take a look here:
https://www.3drudder.com/

When I designed MerperVR, I focused on a room-scale experience because that felt the most natural and therefore the better use of the technology.  Using the 3DRudder made me re-evaluate that, because it makes seated scenarios compelling in their own way by fixing the locomotion problem.

If you have a small space, or a headset that doesn't quite support room scale I highly recommend you get yourself one.

Cheers,
F

notes.title: v1.0.7 - Welcome Oculus Rift + Touch!
notes.content:
Happy New Year!

I'm happy to welcome [b]Oculus Rift[/b] users to MerperVR!

While this was technically possible before given the OpenVR support ( which still holds true for other headsets ) this release adds Oculus-specific UI to match the touch controllers and positions UI in a way that's easier to use on  a seated experience.

Note that given that this is a manipulation-centric experience, you will still need to have touch controllers. Take a look:

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/6cfd262b4e107c657459fad3997d21682c8a0a37.jpg[/img]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/c8b070c05afa213628b965bee3f4ee68b4ff28ca.jpg[/img]

For everyone else, I tweaked the laser pointers a bit and the way the grip button moves the UI.

Enjoy!
F

notes.title: v1.0.6 - more PBR and uploadable screenshots
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

This version brings the semi-transparent material that lets you see through your models to find their skeletons in line with the main PBR renderer.

It also integrates better with the overall Steam platform, not just SteamVR / OpenVR - this means your screenshots will now be uploadable when you hit the screeshot button in EXPRESS mode.  Please share yours!  

Here's a shot of the new transparent material that I also uploaded to the screenshots section:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/73e9fe556de1919dd28918f38b8731769f33b053.png[/img]

There's also a litte update for those of you without VR - as mentioned before, the game will run outside of a VR context, it's just not very usable without the head tracking and motion controllers.  Still, I added WSAD keyboard support for non-VR environment so you can move around the UI.

And for those of you who want to try it and don't have the right system requirements ( 99.9% of the time your GPU does not support OpenGL 4.5 ) you'll get a more descriptive error message before the application exits.

Enjoy!

F

notes.title: v1.0.5 - Improved Environments
notes.content:
Hello All,

This patch adds a few more HDR environment maps and defaults to use higher resolution ones by default.  

For the generated enviroments the sky model uses a single scattering simulation of a physical atmosphere.

The lighting now takes into account the average luminance of the environment which results in a better range and overal cleaner looks.

Enjoy!

F

notes.title: Version 1.0.3 is out
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

I've been working on improving the visual quality for this release. Everything should look more in line with the environment, be more physically correct and feel a whole lot brighter. 

As part of that, I also added a button to load a custom .HDR environment maps next to the standard four, and added a few more 1k CC0 files from the awesome HDRHAVEN site: 

https://hdrihaven.com 

I highly suggest that you go there and get some of the higher qualiky ones ( I'm posting a few pictures using their 4k files ) and if you like please support them, they do an excellent job.

Of couse you are free lo load any .HDR file you want as long as it is in lat/lon 2:1 aspect. 

The simulated environments have not changed much, but the new lighting should make them more usable, particularly the sunset one.

The UI is now on the far Z plane, or in other words rotated 90 degrees from where it was.  This is as a starting point to support other headsets which tend to look in that direction as the default.  If you happen to have a Windows headset or an Oculus, please try it out. 

As always, please post your comments on the forums.

Thanks,
F

The Ghost model using one of the new environments
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/36f8bae20d883b0eb590a90c8747301217647d65.png[/img]
Model:
https://sketchfab.com/models/c962d50655e1496581289703a0067b66
Env: 
https://hdrihaven.com/hdri/?c=nature&h=sunny_vondelpark

The MakeHuman female char on one of the 4k environments
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30958757/33b610ba7c573e5494c99246bd6165a3cb005c73.png[/img]
